title: You create your environment
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: If you don't like the result, what in the oven would you change?
I said there is a bit of truth that you are the product of your environment, but you are also in control of creating that environment.

A student agreed and gave an image. If you bake cookies at four hundred fifty degrees for an hour you get hockey pucks. Change the exposure, twelve minutes at three twenty-five, and you get perfect cookies. The cookie is the product, the oven the environment, the time and heat the exposure.
Change even a minute detail and you get a completely different product, the student said.
I asked: who is the positive force in your life, and who is the negative one? A student said they now had a new purpose, a child, and were preparing to provide a safety net.

As we get older we develop deep relationships, I said. Every one of my friends has one common denominator: we were dedicated parents, not by paying for the best schools, but by the amount of time and the deep relationships we built with our children.

I know I'm going to have a successful business relationship when we see eye to eye on parenting, I said. When I haven't, it has been a disaster. The two don't have to correlate, but in my experience, people who aren't good parents are a warning sign for me.

A student said it comes down to core values: the personal mission statement has core values in it, and building a business is almost the same archetype as raising a child. You start when it's nothing and groom it into what it will be. It's an alignment of core values.

A student shared what a mentor once told them: creatives need time to do nothing in order to be creative. Not a full vacation, but time to let the juices flow. Sometimes a little boredom helps you find what inspires you next.
I said: it's all a balance.
What would you change about your oven?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write the environment that shaped you.
Write what in it you would change: heat, time, people.
Write your core values in three words.
Write how your values show up at home and at work.
Write when you last had time to do nothing, and when you will next.

check.q: What did I say about environment?
choices: You are a product of it, but you are in control of creating it

check.q: In the student's cookie image, what is the environment?
What did the student's mentor say creatives need?

recap: You can build your environment. Align your values. Leave room for nothing.
